Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Name: Fake Assets
Cardtype: Action
Discipline: Chimerstry
Cost: 1 blood
+1 stealh action.
[chi] Put this card into play and untap this vampire. During your untap phase, if you've lost 6 or more pool from bleed since your last untap phase, gain 1 pool.
[CHI] As above, and a minion that successfully bleeds you for 4 or more doesn't untap as normal during his or her next untap phase.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
The general concept is good, but I fear it's too narrow. Not all deck bleed you for that kind of amount, and if they oust you outright the card is useless.

Also, you need quite a lot of thoses to have a reasonable chance of seeing one before being at less than 10 pool. It's not unique, but it does not stack very well either, and unlike bounce or bleed reduction you need it well before being in the red zone.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Ankha wrote:
> Name: Fake Assets
> Cardtype: Action
> Discipline: Chimerstry
> Cost: 1 blood
> +1 stealh action.
> [chi] Put this card into play and untap this vampire. During your untap phase, if you've lost 6 or more pool from bleed since your last untap phase, gain 1 pool.
> [CHI] As above, and a minion that successfully bleeds you for 4 or more doesn't untap as normal during his or her next untap phase.
>
Interesting and  as I opined over here some time ago, I'd love to see some more diverse bleed defence in other disciplines. Not to make the game harder for bleed decks than it is when facing a table of 3 Dominate users and an Auspex bouncer, but so that those three Dominate-using decks aren't all feeling forced to graft on Dominate bleed bounce.

Overall, it feels a bit too weak, particularly at inferior. Not unplayable, given the free untap, but probably not enough to make me think about really using it. The superior also has the annoyance of hitting the occasional big bleeder relatively hard, when - say - a consistent Threats + stealth bleeding you for 3 per vampire is never hit. So it could hurt a toolbox deck that gets the occasional bleed off more than the consistent, frequent bleeder. (Of course, it does also hit bona-fide bleedzookas.)

What is interesting is that the inferior pool gain stacks, so - potentially - with X of these in play, I could be getting X pool back each turn. But it's still pretty weak. It's not going to discourage anyone from bleeding me really, unless they have an additional bleed for 1 to take themselves from 5 to 6. (Typically, why waste the action?) It's not generally going to be fast enough to help me.

I might be more interested if, say, it got a counter whenever a bleed resolved against you. (Or maybe "You may add a counter..." to avoid arguments about "Well, it was mandatory for me to put the counter on, but I forgot, so here are four more counters." See arguments over gaining pool from the Edge when it was mandatory.) Then, based on the number of counters, you might be able to do something. And maybe the counters disappear, or trickle off slowly. So you can hit the weenie deck that's bleeding you 5 times and you can hit the Turbo-Arika deck, but less so the toolbox deck that really wants to play a superior Conditioning every so often. Maybe if there are several counters on the card, bleedss against you are automatically at -1 bleed, or cost an extra blood or life, or cause the acting Methuselah to discard cards from their hand if successful, or something like that. So something like "If there are X (three?) or more counters on this card... Burn all the counters during your untap phase" or "If there are X or more counters on this card... Burn two counters during your untap phase."

Possibly, make it a "Put this card on this vampire.... Burn this card when this vampire leaves the ready region" type ability.

Just as a book-keeping issue on the card as it stands. This could be annoying if, say, you play it out-of-turn. So I play it during my predator's minion phase, after I've been bled, and then we argue about whether you bled me for 5 or 6 this turn. Maybe put counters on the card as the bleed resolves, that sort of thing.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
There are plenty of interesting idea above.

The main goal of the card was to buy some time against a heavy bleeder deck. For instance, a deck that would require time to set up can slow down a little a DOM or DEM bleeder. It is absolutely not meant to be an auto include but fits only some decks that need some time to set up as I said.

May be it lacks something extra to make it worth a slot, like:

Name: Fake Assets
Cardtype: Reaction/Action
Discipline: Chimerstry
Cost: 1 blood
[REACTION][chi] Reduce a bleed against you by 2.
[ACTION][chi] +1 stealh action. Put this card into play and untap this vampire. During your untap phase, if you've lost 6 or more pool from bleed since your last untap phase, gain 1 pool.
[ACTION][CHI] As above, and a minion that successfully bleeds you for 4 or more doesn't untap as normal during his or her next untap phase.

Prince of Paris, France
